ctx.x: Irving Mills, and later on he decided to give me a percentage, and thank God, at least I got something from Caravan, but since I sold it outright, I didn't

have no business getting nothing, but later on in the years, he gave me a percentage on Caravan, which has been the two best things for me -- that was Caravan and Perdifo. And that old sonofabitch, that sister of Duke Ellington, you know -- she was the one who messed me up.

items.title: 61531_Juan Tizol oral history interview
items.q: I know he was working for Duke and Irving Mills in the publishing company.

ctx.x: The lyric writer, perhaps, of Lost in Meditation, was Singer. There are four names; Tizol, Ellington, Singer and Mills. In Lost in Meditation. Singer? S-i-n-g-e-r.
I know he was working for Duke and Irving Mills in the publishing company.

items.title: 61531_Juan Tizol oral history interview
items.q: But Temple wanted me to sue him.

ctx.x: No. They asked me why I don't sue him, but he had been stealing numbers from everybody, so then he was allowed later on, to sue me, so I said, oh, well,
" forget it." But Temple wanted me to sue him.
I guess I remember you and Duke talking about it.
